description: The import-fidelity oracle wiring (issue #332, story Sf-2 of the full real-file-import epic). The epic's exit criterion asks that a real imported file render inside a measured tolerance band of Figma's own GET /images render, but the epic's two real targets are third-party Community files, and docs/decisions/figma-corpus-self-authored-only.md forbids committing their JSON or their render — their fidelity is checked live only (`just render`). This manifest carries the committed, license-clean half: two self-authored fixtures that exercise the two vocabulary paths the real import proved live but no E7 oracle frame measures — an embedded image fill, and the #310 text axes end-to-end. Per frame the oracle imports the committed fixture (corpus/figma-fixtures/<name>.json) with its committed image bytes (<name>.images/), narrows it to the single canvas node the design source is an export of (the frame's figmaNodeId — a captured fixture is the whole file, and dashc lowers every top-level canvas node as an independent root re-based to the origin, so an unexported sibling would paint over the measured frame; debt #382), compiles it through dashc's compile_figma (Profile::Core), renders the emitted .dsb through goldens::render::render_dsb (the Sf-1 render path: measure seam, text axes, embedded images), and diffs that fresh render against the committed Figma design-source PNG within the frame's band. The bands are the E7 oracle's three pinned rules (goldens/tooling/src/oracle.rs), reused read-only — never retuned here. The diff runs in goldens/tooling/tests/import_oracle.rs. This manifest is deliberately separate from goldens/oracle/manifest.json: that file, its design-source/ directory, and its test are the live v0.9 E7 exit gate and are never touched by the import oracle. A frame is captured by `deno task import-oracle-capture` (importers/figma), which downloads Figma's GET /images render into import-design-source/<frame>.png and flips the frame's designSource and status to captured.

frames.note: One fixed 400x200 FRAME whose only paint is an IMAGE fill with scaleMode FILL — the image decode -> embed -> paint path the hero target (Landify's phone mockups) exercised live, unmeasured by any E7 frame. The image is a self-generated 380x380 RGBA PNG (gradients, two hard-edged rectangles, a semi-transparent square; the alpha channel keeps Figma from re-encoding the upload to JPEG, which the PNG-only v0.3 image table refuses). The 380x380 image in the 400x200 box means FILL scales the paint up to cover and crops it vertically, so the diff also measures the scale-and-crop path — the way the hero's mockups actually use image fills. The reference render decodes the committed image bytes from the fixture's .images/ directory, embedded into the .dsb at compile (dashbuf Image { bytes }). Measured 263/80000 px (0.329%, max delta 89) — rect-edge anti-aliasing and sub-threshold resampling noise, within the aa-edge band.

One fixed 400x200 FRAME with a single TEXT node in Noto Sans Regular 24 exercising the #310 text axes end-to-end through the #327/#334 render wiring: PIXELS line height 18, letter spacing 1.2, textAlignHorizontal RIGHT, textAlignVertical BOTTOM, in a fixed 352x165 text box larger than its content so both alignments displace the block visibly. Authored in Noto Sans (the committed corpus/atlas/ascii font), so the diff measures the reference painter against Figma's render of the SAME font, not a substitution (the text-latin/text-baseline precedent). This frame caught two real bugs on its first measurement (2.822%, structurally misplaced): an absent textAutoResize mis-lowered as auto-size, collapsing the fixed box (dashc), and a fixed line height placing the baseline at the full intrinsic ascent instead of centering the intrinsic box within the fixed line box (half-leading, dashscene-typeset) — the run sat 7 px below Figma's. Fixed, it measured 1463/80000 px (1.829%, max delta 255): glyph edges plus ~1 px of horizontal placement from the trailing letter-spacing step Figma excludes from the measured width. That step was then dropped from the measured width (#336, PR #372), which tightened this frame to 823/80000 px (1.029%) — glyph edges alone. The msdf-text band.

One fixed 160x160 FRAME whose only paint is an opaque IMAGE fill (scaleMode FILL) whose bytes are a real baseline JPEG (magic FF D8 FF, ends FF D9, 16x16) — the JPEG image-fill vocabulary path (story #342): dashpaint::ImageFormat::Jpeg decoded through the Skia reference painter's own codec. Self-authored with the fixture-author plugin's jpeg-fill command (importers/figma/plugin/fixture-author/README.md); no asset placed through the UI. Measured 0/25600 px (0.000%, max delta 0) — an exact match, well within the aa-edge band.

One FRAME holding two TEXT nodes in Noto Sans, the same string 'waffle finish office' set twice — liga-off carrying Figma's standard-ligatures-off OpenType flag (style.opentypeFlags {"LIGA":0}), liga-on at the font default — the ligatures_off text axis lowered by story #341 (epic #343). Self-authored with the fixture-author plugin's liga-text command (importers/figma/plugin/fixture-author/README.md) plus the manual ligature toggle the Plugin API cannot write. Measured 6/84000 px (0.007%, max delta 60) — an effectively exact match: the ligature substitution reproduces Figma's own shaping, and the residual is six glyph-edge pixels. The msdf-text band is kept because the band names the KIND of residual a frame carries (a text frame's glyph edges), not its magnitude; bands are reused read-only and never retuned. This frame previously recorded 1907/84000 px (2.270%): debt #382 found that the fixture's `1:5 _manual-checklist` — the fixture-author plugin's authoring-instruction annotation, a canvas SIBLING of the frame at y=224, outside the 0..200 region Figma exports — was lowered by dashc as its own root re-based to the origin and painted over the measured frame, so 1901 of those 1907 differing pixels were annotation ink the design source cannot contain. The oracle now narrows every fixture to the single node its design source exports (figmaNodeId) before compiling, so the number measures the frame.

One fixed 460x160 FRAME with four filled VECTOR nodes (star-5-point NONZERO, arrow NONZERO, organic-blob cubic Béziers NONZERO, square-with-hole EVENODD) — the baked-vector lowering path (story B1/#340): each VECTOR's fillGeometry lowers through dashc to an fdsm MSDF field packed into a shared atlas (geometry=paths fetch, B1.4), rendered as a field quad through the Skia painter's median-of-3 coverage resolve (B1.3). The msdf-text band: a baked MSDF field rendered as a quad is the same reconstruction as an msdf-text glyph — median-of-3, sharp high-contrast edges — so its residual vs Figma's exact path raster is glyph-edge-like (sub-pixel AA disagreement along curved edges), the residual the msdf-text band was tuned for, reused read-only and never retuned. Re-authored with the fixtureShapes stroke-clear plugin fix (importers/figma/plugin/fixture-author/code.js): the frame rebuilt at node 3:2, its four vectors now fill-only (SOLID, no stroke), so dashc lowers all four cleanly. Measured 1/73600 px (0.001%, max delta 61) against Figma's GET /images render — effectively an exact match, comfortably inside the msdf-text band; the earlier 2.935% figure was an artifact of the still-stroked source's black outline inflating the diff, not the baked-vector lowering's own fidelity.

expectedWarnings: node rotation is not in the document vocabulary yet
frames.note: One fixed 540x160 FRAME with four node-effects lowering paths (story C2/#143, epic #343): a rotated rectangle, a half-opacity rectangle, a hidden layer (visible:false), and a mask pair (an isMask ellipse masking a rectangle). Node opacity, box-outline masks, and hidden nodes already lower (v0.8 story #44, debt #143) — this frame is the committed replay+measurement for that lowering, not a new dashc un-pin. One disclosed hole, excluded from the diff and named here rather than hidden inside the band: the rotated rectangle. Rotation stays refused by design (zero non-axis-aligned relativeTransform in either real-file target, no rotation schema in v0.10), a permanent hole; its excludeRegion is Figma's own reported absoluteBoundingBox for the rotated node, ceil/floor-rounded to the covering integer pixel box. The mask pair's hole is closed (debt #361): the fixture-author plugin was corrected to build the mask shape as a full circle with maskType VECTOR, a human re-ran the node-fx command, and this capture is the result — the mask now lowers, so its excludeRegion and its two expectedWarnings entries are gone and the frame is measured over the mask pair as well. Re-running the command deletes and rebuilds the frame, so its node id changed from 1:2 to 7:9 and figmaNodeId above was updated with it. Hard-edged rectangles and a circle: the aa-edge band. Measured 5/71271 px (0.007%, max delta 49) over the opacity+hidden+mask result, against 0/61271 px (0.000%, max delta 2) before the mask pair was included — the measured area grew by exactly the mask pair's 100x100 box, and the five differing pixels are the circle's antialiased edge, which is what the aa-edge band exists for.

One fixed FRAME holding one RECTANGLE with two visible fills — an opaque SOLID at fills[0] (the bottom layer) and a semi-transparent GRADIENT_LINEAR at fills[1] (opacity 0.55, stacked on top) — for the stacked-fills vocabulary path (story C1/#146, epic #343): dashc's paint_of lowers the fills array in order onto PaintEntry.fill/extra_fills, and dashpaint/dashscene-skia composite them bottom to top on the same box. The aa-edge band: the content is a hard-edged rect with a flat-shaded gradient overlay, not msdf-like or blurred, so the expected residual is rect-edge anti-aliasing and gradient-interpolation rounding — the same residual class as the image-fill and jpeg-fill frames above, both measured in this band. Measured 0/40000 px (0.000%, max delta 2) — effectively an exact match, well within the aa-edge band.

One fixed 520x240 VERTICAL auto-layout FRAME (padding 24, itemSpacing 16) holding three TEXT rows, the same string 'Sphinx of quartz 123' at size 28 in Noto Sans Regular 400, SemiBold 600 and Bold 700 — the per-weight face selection path (story #368, epic #344): the typesetter picks a face by CSS weight and the render walk stages each run against that weight's committed atlas (corpus/atlas/ascii, ascii-semibold, ascii-bold). A weight ladder makes the failure signature unmistakable: with weight selection broken all three rows render identically to each other while Figma's three differ visibly, so the diff would be large and structural, not glyph-edge-sized. Authored in Noto Sans, not Inter, so the diff measures our per-weight atlas selection against Figma's render of the SAME family at the SAME weight — never a family substitution (the text-latin/import-text-axes precedent); family substitution stays out of scope. Figma's REST style.fontPostScriptName is null on all three rows, so the metadata cannot confirm that three distinct faces were applied; it was confirmed empirically instead, on Figma's own render, by counting non-background pixels inside each row's reported absoluteBoundingBox: 2001 px (Regular), 2552 px (SemiBold), 2902 px (Bold), strictly increasing by 551 and 350 px — a heavier face lays down measurably more ink for the same string at the same size. Figma's three reported row widths (271, 280, 285) differ for the same reason. The null PostScript name is therefore a Figma REST metadata gap, not a substitution. Measured 1308/124800 px (1.048%, max delta 211) — glyph edges only, comparable to import-text-axes' 1.029%, within the msdf-text band, reused read-only and never retuned. The render emitted no text.weight-substituted diagnostic, so all three weights resolved to an exact committed face.

One fixed 320x180 FRAME carrying the first BACKGROUND_BLUR the corpus measures (story #393, docs/decisions/backdrop-blur-is-core-vocabulary.md): three hard-edged vertical bands (amber 0-107, navy 107-213, pale 213-320), a 72x72 ELLIPSE at x 124-196 sitting entirely inside the navy band, and a 200x90 frosted panel at (60,45) — corner radius 16, white at 0.2 alpha, BACKGROUND_BLUR radius 16 — which straddles both seams and the circle. Self-authored with the fixture-author plugin's backdrop-blur command; fully scripted, so the file carries no _manual-checklist canvas sibling (debt #382), and image-free. The frame lowers with no diagnostic: backdrop blur became core vocabulary in stage B-1, and the Skia reference painter honours it in stage B-3. Measured 10/57600 px (0.017%, max delta 51) against Figma's GET /images render. The band is classified from the residual, never from expectation — the rule v08-baseline established. Every differing pixel lies within 0.5 px of the ELLIPSE's rim and above the panel's top edge (y <= 44 < 45), where the reference painter's coverage rounding and Figma's server-side export resampling disagree; that is what the aa-edge band names, and the same residual class as the import-image-fill, jpeg-fill, node-fx and stacked-fills frames. The blurred region contributes nothing to the count: inside the panel's 200x90 box the largest per-channel delta is 16 and the mean is 2.70, with zero pixels over either threshold. Everything that is neither the circle's rim nor the panel is pixel-exact (max delta 0). Counted at blur-falloff's tighter delta-24 threshold the frame differs by 43/57600 px (0.075%), and those 43 are the same rim. The band also decides whether the frame can fail. Measured with the fixture's BACKGROUND_BLUR stripped and nothing else changed, the render differs by 3123/57600 px (5.422%, max delta 91) at the aa-edge threshold — past this band's 2% budget — so a dropped blur fails this frame. The same no-blur render measures 4869/57600 px (8.453%) at blur-falloff's threshold, INSIDE blur-falloff's 12% budget, so that band would have stayed green with the blur removed (setting the panel's visible to false reproduces the no-blur render byte for byte). AA-EDGE DOES NOT DOMINATE BLUR-FALLOFF, and this note should not be read as saying so. It is tighter on area (2% against 12%) but 67% more permissive per pixel (delta 40 against 24), which is the wrong direction for low-amplitude wide-area error. Measured by sweeping the panel's fill alpha from its authored 0.20: at 0.30 aa-edge sees 10 px (0.017%, pass) while blur-falloff sees 5826 px (10.115%, pass); at 0.35 aa-edge sees 243 px (0.422%, still pass) while blur-falloff sees 13570 px (23.559%, fail). blur-falloff catches an error class aa-edge is blind to. aa-edge is chosen because the measured residual is hard-edge anti-aliasing and the rule is to follow the residual, not because it is the stricter band. WHAT THIS FRAME DOES NOT PIN. It does not pin the sigma mapping: the headline 10/57600 is identical for every painter sigma from 4 to 10 against the authored radius 16, so anything in [radius/4, 3*radius/4] stays green on both bands. Within that window sigma = 7 fits Figma measurably better than the shipped radius/2 = 8 (panel mean 1.187 against 2.704, RMS 1.545 against 3.652), which suggests Figma's BACKGROUND_BLUR is nearer 0.42-0.45*radius than 0.5*radius — debt #412, not settled here. It does not pin the paint-order barrier: painting the panel before the ellipse, so the blur samples the wrong backdrop, measures 1005 px (1.745%) and passes, with only 0.255 points of margin. And it exercises only the parametric path: this panel is a FRAME, so it renders through draw_backdrop_blur_box, while the live hero's frosted panel is a Figma VECTOR and renders through draw_backdrop_blur_field, a different function with its own clip and coverage-mask confinement. No committed frame measures that path — debt #413.

One fixed 320x180 FRAME carrying a BACKGROUND_BLUR on a baked VECTOR (debt #413): a frosted ring (outer r=64, hole r=32, white at 0.2 alpha, BACKGROUND_BLUR radius 16) centred in the frame at (160,90), over a backdrop identical to the backdrop-blur frame's — three hard-edged bands (seams at x=107 and x=213) and a 72x72 ELLIPSE at x 124-196. Self-authored with the fixture-author plugin's vector-backdrop-blur command; fully scripted, image-free, and it lowers with no diagnostic. WHY A SECOND BLUR FRAME. The Skia painter renders a frosted FRAME through draw_backdrop_blur_box and a frosted VECTOR through draw_backdrop_blur_field, because a rounded-rect clip cannot express a baked outline. Only the second is the path the live hero's frosted panel takes. The backdrop is identical to backdrop-blur's by construction (both plugin commands call blurBackdrop), so the two frames differ in exactly one thing and their residuals are directly comparable. Measured 19/57600 px (0.033%, max delta 64) against Figma's GET /images render. THE RESIDUAL IS MIXED, and the note says so rather than claiming one component is absent. All 19 pixels that cross the aa-edge threshold are the ELLIPSE's anti-aliased rim: every one lies within 0.33 px of that circle's radius, 12 where the rim crosses the ring's hole and 7 where it falls outside the ring's quad. But the frame also carries an MSDF-class residual on the ring's own coverage edge (n=1104, mean 5.60, max 33, 56 pixels over blur-falloff's threshold) and a blur-falloff-class residual across the ring body (n=8744, mean 4.42). Both stay under the aa-edge threshold; neither is nil. Means are max-over-RGBA, the same metric the pass/fail counts use. THE BAND IS CHOSEN ON THE KIND OF RESIDUAL, NOT ON WHICH COMPONENT HAPPENS TO CROSS A THRESHOLD. Arguing aa-edge from 'the MSDF edge contributes zero pixels above delta 40' would be circular — it uses aa-edge's own threshold to justify aa-edge, and that edge contributes zero above msdf-text's threshold too, so the test does not discriminate. The kind argument is this: msdf-text is scoped by its own definition to sharp high-contrast transitions in sparse text ink, and vector-shapes took it because four opaque filled vectors are exactly that. This frame's MSDF boundary is the opposite — a low-contrast, large-area coverage edge on a 0.2-alpha fill over a blurred backdrop (measured design-source contrast across the ring rim is a median of 50, against 200 across the ELLIPSE rim) — and what the frame exists to measure is where a blur stops, not how glyph-like ink reconstructs. It also puts this frame in the same band as the twin it is meant to be compared against. AND THE MSDF EDGE IS NOT THE MORE ACCURATE ONE. An earlier draft of this note argued that our ring reconstruction agrees with Figma better than our ELLIPSE rasterisation because its max delta is 33 against the ellipse's 64. That comparison is wrong: normalised by each edge's own contrast the MSDF edge disagrees about 3.3 times more on average (0.112 against 0.034 of contrast) and twice as much at worst. It stays under the threshold because it is a low-contrast edge, not because it is better reconstructed. WHAT THIS FRAME WOULD HAVE TO CONTAIN TO FAIL, measured by rendering each mutation rather than argued. Removing the DstIn coverage mask from draw_backdrop_blur_field, so the blur fills the padded field quad (149x149 at (85,15), not the shape's 128x128 bounding box) instead of following the outline: 6.729%, with 1659 px in the quad's corners, 1127 outside the 128x128 box, 787 in the hole, 261 on the ring rim, 42 on the hole rim. Confining it to the node's literal bounding box instead: 4.785%. Dropping the blur entirely: 4.295%. Losing the EVENODD hole so the ring bakes as a disc: 3.849%. All four fail the 2% budget. The band choice again decides whether the frame can fail: the first three mutations measure 9.302%, 6.819% and 6.606% at blur-falloff's threshold, all INSIDE its 12% budget. msdf-text would catch three of the four but let the lost hole through at 2.245%, and would pass a dropped blur by only 0.207 points. WHAT THIS FRAME DOES NOT PIN. It does not catch the defect PR #403 fixed. That was a missing clip_rect that left the layer over the whole device clip, and it measures 1.585% here — inside the 2% budget, because 901 of its 913 differing pixels fall outside the quad where the backdrop is flat. That regression is covered by the unit test the_baked_vector_blur_is_confined_to_its_quad, not by this frame, and the frame should not be described as guarding it. It does not pin the sigma mapping: the measurement is exactly 19 px for every painter sigma from 4 to 9 against the authored radius 16, the same blind spot the backdrop-blur frame records, and at blur-falloff's threshold the residual minimises near 0.375-0.44*radius rather than the shipped 0.5 (corroborating debt #412). It does not pin paint order: drawing the ring before the dot, so the blur samples the wrong backdrop, measures 1.149% and passes. At this band the frame is a confinement test, not a blur-quality test.
